headline: High: Dify’s writable, broad-egress orchestration can feed OpenMetadata’s MCP/API surface, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can write/read files and call user-defined OpenAPI tools, while OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible content bridge where Dify-produced or stored content can be consumed by OpenMetadata workflows as instructions or metadata. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are routed into OpenMetadata ingestion, webhook, or MCP inputs without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata parses Dify-originated text as trusted metadata or commands, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all Dify-originated payloads before OpenMetadata ingestion.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in ingested text.
Restrict OpenMetadata MCP/webhook consumers to allowlisted schemas.
Review one sample Dify-to-OpenMetadata payload for instruction-like content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, and it has broad network egress plus file access. OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If Dify content is forwarded into OpenMetadata, sensitive operational context can leak across systems even without an explicit shared filesystem. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files are synced into OpenMetadata, sensitive content can be duplicated into governance stores.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP outputs are sent onward, Dify-originated secrets may be exposed to additional services.
mitigations: Remove secrets from Dify knowledge-base uploads.
Limit OpenMetadata ingestion to metadata-only fields for Dify sources.
Rotate any API keys that were present in Dify conversations.
Audit one recent Dify-to-OpenMetadata sync for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and broad network egress; OpenMetadata supports APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Both can mutate shared external resources if wired to the same backend or workflow, so overlapping writes are plausible. There is no documented locking or coordination between them, and the uncertainty should be treated conservatively as medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same catalog, ticket, or file-backed workspace, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Dify workflows and OpenMetadata jobs target the same mutable resource without locks, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate namespaces or directories to each agent.
Pause one writer during bulk syncs.
Check for duplicate updates on a single sample record.
Use optimistic version checks where available.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can wire tools into agent/workflow apps, and OpenMetadata is a data-governance/catalog system that can act on APIs, events, and webhooks. That makes it plausible for Dify outputs to become authoritative inputs for OpenMetadata actions without a verification step. Because downstream actions can affect governance state or trigger workflows, the blast radius is potentially broad and irreversible.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata consumes Dify-generated facts without human or rule-based verification, incorrect outputs can propagate into governance records.
IF Dify triggers OpenMetadata webhooks or API actions from unvalidated model output, cascading errors can affect multiple downstream systems.
mitigations: Insert a manual approval step before OpenMetadata writes.
Require schema validation on all Dify outputs.
Compare one Dify-generated record against source-of-truth data.
Disable auto-action webhooks for untrusted inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates and rollback for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles model provider API keys, tool credentials, conversation logs, and knowledge-base content, while OpenMetadata stores governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data. If regulated or sensitive content from Dify is ingested into OpenMetadata, retention and residency obligations can diverge across systems. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty prevents a higher severity, but the compliance mismatch pathway is real.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs contain regulated data and OpenMetadata retains them under a different policy, retention mismatch occurs.
IF either system stores EU PII or PHI without matching controls, compliance obligations may be breached.
mitigations: Classify one sample Dify record before syncing.
Set a short retention window for copied logs.
Exclude secrets from OpenMetadata ingestion.
Document the data-residency path for both systems.
requires-engineering: align retention, deletion, and residency controls across the integration.
